newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-INCREASE IN WORLD CUP TEAMS DISMISSED BY FIFA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INCREASE IN WORLD CUP TEAMS DISMISSED BY FIFA.

text.p: FIFA, soccer's world governing body, on Wednesday dismissed as wishful thinking reports that the 2002 World Cup final tournament would increase from 32 teams to 40.
"It's pie in the sky," FIFA spokesman Keith Cooper said. "It's an idea the Japanese have been quoted about in Japan but they have not discussed it with FIFA.
"The regulations are not determined by organisers, only by FIFA. Absolutely nothing has been tabled for discussion. I mean we only just increased the World Cup to 32 teams."
Twenty-four teams took part in the 1994 World Cup finals in the United States. The number will increase to 32 for the 1998 tournament in France.

Japan and South Korea, who will jointly host the 2002 World Cup, were making what FIFA termed unscheduled "courtesy calls" on Wednesday and Thursday this week. The subject of increasing the number of teams was not on the agenda.
The issue, however, could be brought up at meetings on November 6 when FIFA meets the co-hosts to begin sorting out the problems of staging the World Cup in two countries for the first time.
